label: Late original positions / <DEL> step of long sequences, gated by first token and current input
explanation: Fires only in the original and delimiter phases and never in the copy phase. About half its mass is on the <DEL> step and half on the last few original positions (orig_idx 6-8, t = 7-9), so it is almost entirely in L = 8-9 sequences (93% of mass). Within that window it is content-selective: rate is about 4x higher when the first original token is t/d/k (also r, 3, 2, p, i), and on original steps it prefers inputs b, z, 0, n, e, q, g, f (b is the strongest, and the top activations are b/z just before <DEL>). It is rare on w/u/h inputs. It mostly fires on first occurrences (in_first, 91% of mass). The position window alone gives recall 0.84 but precision 0.11. Adding the first-token and input-token lists brings dev F1 to 0.48 (mass recall 0.67), and the strongest activations are better covered (top-quartile coverage about 0.97 for the position-only predicate). The token lists are empirical, so the unit looks like a distributed, content-dependent code rather than one clean concept.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: t, d, k, 3, r, 2; least: z, n, 0, e) and the current input token, by phase (input phase: b, z, 0, n; delimiter step: <DEL>; copy phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=8, t=8, t=7.
